To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean torque obtained in a mixer torque experiment can be related to the degree of liquid saturation of the lactose agglomerates and that the mean torque is dependent on the massing time, the binder concentration, the binder viscosity, the particle size of the binder and the mixer type.
the melt agglom-eration properties of PEG 30000 are very similar to those of PEG 2000.

a longer massing time, a smaller particle size of PEG, and a higher viscosity of the binder resulted in a faster rise in mean torque, and that the binder concentration could be increased without causing overwetted agglomerates, the range being larger with PEG 2000 than with PGE 20 000.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental method to study the melt agglom-eration process in a mixer torque instrument, which is a simple, inexpensive, and easy-to-handle apparatus.
the evaluation of the melt agglomera- tion process in a mixer torque rhcometer.
the melt agglom-eration of lactose in the mixer torque rheometer using different poly-ethylene glycols as meltable binders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mixer torque rheometer is not a suitable instrument for predicting melt agglomerations in a high shear granulator.
the mixer torque rheometer can be a useful tool in the development of melt agglomerates if the experiments are performed under carefully controlled experimental conditions.

the melt agglom-eration properties of a meltable binder are strongly influenced by the experimental conditions and that the melt agglomer-ation properties of a mel-table binder in one type of mixer cannot be predicted from experiments in another type of mixer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mixer torque rheometer is useful for studying the melt agglom-eration process, but it should be realized that the results cannot be directly transferred to a high shear mixer.
the mixer torque rheometer is useful as a screening tool for the evaluation of melt agglomerating properties of binders, but that the results should be interpreted with care.
a mixer torque rheometric method for the evaluation of melt agglomerates is feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the melt agglomera-tion properties of PEGs are very dependent on the binder concentration and the binder viscosity.
the mixer torque rheometer can be used to evaluate the melt agglomera- tion properties of PEGs in a low shear mixer.
the melt agglom-eration process is highly sensitive to the experimental conditions and that the melt agglomerated particles are highly porous.
